observation_summary: The ConstructorInstantiator failed to instantiate inner classes because it was hardcoded to look for a constructor matching only the outer class instance type, failing to account for other potential constructor parameters or variations in inner class instantiation.
hypothesis: The instantiation logic was too restrictive, assuming a specific constructor signature (only the outer class instance). The fix replaces this rigid lookup with a more flexible search that iterates through all available constructors and validates parameter types dynamically.
prediction: The code will now iterate through all declared constructors of the target class, check if the provided parameters match the constructor's parameter types, and invoke the matching constructor.
experiment_rationale: The diff shows the removal of a hardcoded constructor lookup (`cls.getDeclaredConstructor(outerClassInstance.getClass())`) and the introduction of a loop over all constructors combined with a `paramsMatch` helper method. This is a fundamental change to the procedural logic of how the class is instantiated.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves rewriting the procedural logic for finding and invoking a constructor. It moves from a single, rigid lookup to a flexible search-and-match algorithm. This is a classic 'Algorithm/Method' fix because it corrects the computational strategy for object instantiation without requiring a design-level change to the class structure or interface contracts.
evidence_used: The diff replaces 'withOuterClass' (which used a single hardcoded constructor lookup) with 'withParams' (which iterates through all constructors).
The addition of 'paramsMatch' helper method to validate constructor parameters dynamically.
The stack trace indicates an 'InstantationException' occurring during the constructor lookup process.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix changes how the constructor is invoked, the root cause is the internal logic of the 'ConstructorInstantiator' class, not a mismatch in the interface contract between two components.
The fix is a local procedural improvement to an existing instantiation mechanism, not the addition of a missing design-level capability or class.
